name: Technoliberalism
summary: Technoliberalism is the belief that networked technology can reconcile economic liberalism with social liberalism, delivering both prosperity and social well-being. It prefers decentralized, participatory and open systems to top-down institutions, backs free markets under enforced rules, favors small business over corporate concentration, and supports measures such as a guaranteed minimum income and pollution pricing. Adam Fish, who popularised the term, treats it critically as a left-liberal, deterministic and utopian digital discourse.
scope: The profile combines the Wikipedia description of technoliberalism (liberty, decentralization, faith in technology, small-business capitalism, rules-based markets) with Adam Fish's 2017 analysis of it as a left-liberal digital discourse held by figures like Al Gore and Barack Obama. The source base is thin and rests largely on Fish, so most answers are inferences from liberal and technology-optimist principles; it excludes technolibertarianism and technocracy.

sources.usedFor: Technoliberal paradox, regulation, net neutrality and activism strategy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Wikipedia lists publicly funded education and a guaranteed minimum income, so a left-liberal welfare floor extends plausibly to health care, though no source names it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The ideology prefers a negative income tax or basic income to wage floors, and sources never mention minimum wages, so adherents are split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: It backs free markets only with strongly enforced rules and engineering-style regulation, so it neither endorses nor rejects market superiority flatly.

public-ownership.rationale: Wikipedia stresses decentralization and distrust of top-down institutions, and favors competition over state monopoly; inferred, not stated for utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Sources stress fair taxes on big companies, not wealthy individuals, so an individual wealth-tax stance is not documented.

unions-good.rationale: Fish's account concerns media activists and professionals rather than labor unions; unions are not discussed in the sources.

property-fundamental.rationale: The liberty emphasis is tempered by competition rules on large firms, and the sources do not treat property as nearly inviolable.

regulate-corporations.rationale: It applies stricter competition rules to large firms than small ones and wants multinationals to pay fair taxes, favoring tighter rules on big corporations.

cut-welfare.rationale: It supports a negative income tax or basic income guaranteeing a minimum, which is a welfare floor rather than dependency-driven cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: The sources favor small and medium businesses but never discuss collective worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Its commitment to liberty, individuality, free networked communication and online speech argues against security surveillance, though state surveillance is not addressed directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from a liberty and individuality emphasis and social liberalism; no source addresses drug policy.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: It supports free speech online with minimal controls, which implies skepticism of speech restrictions; hate speech is not addressed.

strong-leader.rationale: It stresses balanced power, decentralization and peer review and distrusts top-down institutions, which contradicts a leader bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: It supports regulation, competition law, publicly funded education and a minimum income, so it is far from regarding the state as unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from left-liberal social orientation and engineering-style governance; sources never discuss firearms.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from liberty and decentralization emphasis and Fish's complaint that states jail hackers; security funding is not discussed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from social liberalism and individual liberty; not addressed in sources.

decide-locally.rationale: Decentralization and local spending with small local firms are core to the Wikipedia description, as is distrust of top-down institutions.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from left-liberal social orientation; criminal justice is not in the sources.

traditional-family.rationale: Described as left-liberal and individualist, it is unlikely to treat traditional family structure as foundational, though sources are silent.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Fish calls it a left-liberal discourse with social liberalism at its core, so this follows by inference; same-sex marriage is not discussed.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from left-liberal social orientation and individual liberty; not discussed.

more-religion-public.rationale: Its faith lies in technology and individual choice, so a larger public religious role is unlikely; inferred only.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Social liberalism in Fish's account aims at social well-being and inclusion, so adherents lean toward active correction; not stated specifically.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Adherents are unlikely to have a settled collective view; the sources do not touch on gender theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Individuality and networked, borderless communication de-emphasize national tradition; inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: It has overriding faith in technology and distrusts conventional modernist institutions, which leans against deference to established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Left-liberal and networked orientation suggests openness to migration; sources do not mention immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Decentralization argues against concentrating power, while global competition and tax cooperation (OECD tax rules) point the other way.

free-trade.rationale: It favors small and local business and aims to weaken global capitalism, but also supports free markets and open internet; sources do not address trade.

nation-first.rationale: The aim of weakening global corporate capitalism is not nationalist, and networked openness is cosmopolitan; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; left-liberal adherents could split between human-rights interventionism and skepticism.

open-borders.rationale: Wikipedia is silent on immigration; adherents' libertarian and left-liberal strands could pull differently.

limit-growth.rationale: It backs emissions trading and pollution costs, a market-and-technology route to environmental goals rather than limiting growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: It supports higher taxes on fossil fuels and environmentally damaging activity, cap and trade and car-free cities.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Wikipedia states technoliberalism holds an overriding faith in technology and expects engagement with it to produce social goods; Fish describes the same faith.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; tech-optimism would favor it while environmental regulation emphasis does not settle the matter.

revolution-justified.rationale: Its model is balanced power, peer review and consultation within existing systems, and Fish's own advice is subversive media-making, not revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Peer review, public consultations and petitions point to citizen engagement; engineering-style governance pulls slightly the other way.

central-planning.rationale: It favors competition, small business and decentralization and distrusts top-down institutions.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not discussed; it favors small private firms in competitive markets, but not on grounds of ownership form.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not discussed; its environmental taxes show openness to resource taxation but no stated view on replacing other taxes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed in sources; adherents are unlikely to share a collective view.

basic-income.rationale: Wikipedia lists a negative income tax to guarantee a minimum income and mentions Universal Basic Income as an example of support.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Favoring open competition and free networked exchange cuts against tariffs, though support for local small business is an opposing pull.

state-directs-investment.rationale: It favors engineering-style regulation and market competition, and distrusts top-down direction; not discussed directly.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Wikipedia says it prefers small and medium business capitalism over corporate capitalism and values local spending with small firms.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: It endorses free markets and capitalism of small firms, so abolishing money and wage labor is far outside it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; it supports rule-bound markets, and would not usually back abolition of monetary institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: It favors decentralization and citizen participation over state-recognized peak bodies; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: It emphasizes balanced power, peer review of decisions and public consultation, which are incompatible with one-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Its decentralizing, participatory and individualist outlook sits poorly with hereditary rule; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: It supports public consultation, petitions and citizen engagement, though it is mostly concerned with technology rather than regime type.

direct-votes.rationale: Wikipedia cites public consultations and petitions as citizen engagement and favors decentralized, participatory decision making.

workers-councils.rationale: Not discussed; its participatory instincts are tech-mediated and compatible with parliaments.

right-to-secede.rationale: Decentralization favors local autonomy but secession is not discussed.

natural-rulers.rationale: Peer review, balance of power and individuality are incompatible with a natural ruling class.

political-violence-never.rationale: Fish urges activists to make subversive media and pursue policy interventions rather than violence; inferred as nonviolent.

war-builds-character.rationale: A liberal, individualist and networked outlook has no militarist elements.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from liberal secular orientation; not stated.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Its faith is in technology and engineering-style governance, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: It wants strongly enforced market rules and balanced power, not privatized justice; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: No stated interest in military primacy; inferred from liberal, decentralist orientation.

ethnic-nation.rationale: An individualist, networked, liberal ideology rejects ethnic definitions of nationhood.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Fish uses a liberal frame with tensions inside liberalism, not class conflict as history's engine, though he is critical of corporate capital.

equal-outcomes.rationale: It emphasizes liberty and a minimum income floor, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The sources never address indigenous land rights, and liberal individualism and decentralization pull in different directions.

civilizational-union.rationale: Its networked and decentralist outlook has no civilizational bloc element; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: It stresses individuality and responsibility alongside social goods, so there is no clear stance on self-interest as moral.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The ideology is built on liberty and individuality.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental policy is market-based and instrumental; intrinsic value is not discussed.

limit-population.rationale: Not discussed; tech optimism leans against population limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Overriding faith in technology makes this rejection central.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Faith in technology and wide availability with minimal controls implies speeding adoption, though it also mentions engineering-style regulation of impact.

human-enhancement.rationale: Technology should be widely available with minimal controls, and it explicitly supports genetic engineering.

algorithmic-government.rationale: It favors engineering-style governance but also public consultation and peer review, which clash with handing decisions to algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Free networked communication, liberty and minimal controls on technology imply support for strong encryption; not stated directly.

restore-past-order.rationale: Its orientation is forward looking and technology driven.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Engineering-style governance and peer review suggest evaluating results; the ideology is itself explicit rather than anti-ideological.

direct-action.rationale: Fish endorses subversive media making and policy engagement, not abandoning elections; inferred as mixed, leaning against.

means-match-ends.rationale: Fish's call to just make the subversive media one wants hints at prefigurative practice, but adherents do not state a general rule.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Overriding faith in technology makes this untenable.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not a position of a market and technology ideology; it supports competitive small business.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A minimum income floor is supported but not distribution by need; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: It supports free markets and business competition.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Fish criticises corporate liberalism but frames the problem as insufficient regulation and funding, not exploitation by profit as such.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Incompatible with balanced power and liberal participation.

collective-farming.rationale: Contrary to small-business capitalism and decentralization.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a technoliberal claim; it keeps capitalism with small firms and rules.

taxation-theft.rationale: It wants companies to pay fair taxes and supports taxes on pollution and a guaranteed minimum income.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberty and individuality fit a harm-based limit on state coercion, though regulation of firms goes beyond a pure harm principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individuality is central but the sources do not discuss group rights.

conscription.rationale: Liberty emphasis suggests opposition; not addressed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: It stresses citizen engagement, consultations and petitions, i.e. voice over exit.

state-as-business.rationale: It favors engineering-style governance and citizen participation, not citizens as customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Fish writes that technoliberalism pairs economic liberalism with social liberalism and a government role in creating the conditions for speaking and being heard.

hereditarian-race.rationale: A left-liberal individualist ideology rejects racial hereditarianism.

organic-representation.rationale: It favors citizen engagement and direct consultation over corporate representation.

total-state.rationale: It stresses liberty, decentralization and individuality.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Incompatible with a liberal, networked, decentralist outlook.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Contradicts peer review, balanced power and public consultation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Faith in engineering and peer review implies belief in checkable knowledge.

universal-morality.rationale: Moral epistemology is not part of the ideology, which concerns technology and governance; adherents are split.

single-common-good.rationale: It stresses pluralism, decentralization and balanced power, suggesting competing interests rather than one rational good.

revive-national-language.rationale: No stated interest; networked cosmopolitan orientation leans against.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Peer review and participation values lean toward it, but its small-business preference does not address corporate governance.

school-vouchers.rationale: It supports publicly funded education but not specifically choice-based vouchers.

economic-freedom.rationale: Fish describes economic liberalism as one half of the ideology, but it is paired with social liberalism, so adherents do not claim political freedom depends on it.

rule-by-example.rationale: The ideology relies on peer review, rules and institutions rather than rulers' virtue.

national-self-determination.rationale: Decentralization sympathizes with self-government, but networked cosmopolitanism cuts against nation-state claims; the sources are silent.

force-without-un.rationale: Not discussed; liberal and decentralist outlook leans against unilateral force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Engineering-style approach and technology faith favor reason, though not stated as exclusive guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Liberal and networked outlook leans against citizen-only entitlement; not addressed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: It supports a negative income tax and basic income, which guarantee income without work tests.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: It values free access to information and education; sacrificing libraries is contrary.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Left-liberal social orientation rejects gendered legal roles.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Fish sees states as favoring corporate interests under neoliberalism but not as an essentially class instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: It supports higher taxes on fossil fuels and cap and trade.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Liberal individualism and networked pluralism lean against enforced assimilation; not discussed.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim foreign to the ideology.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not covered; balance of power and participation could favor PR, but nothing states it.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Left-liberal framing suggests acceptance of structural disadvantage; not stated.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Fish criticises elites who exploit the technoliberal discourse, but not political elites as corrupt in general.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Peer review and accountability themes suggest support; not stated.

night-watchman-state.rationale: It supports regulation, competition law, public education and a minimum income.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Liberalism's social side and its individuality emphasis imply this baseline.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist doctrinal question outside this ideology.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Colonial history is outside the ideology's sources, and left-liberal adherents could go either way.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law is outside the ideology's concerns, and liberal equality and pluralism pull in opposite directions.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from liberal secular orientation and public education emphasis.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine contrary to its decentralism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Consultation, petitions and citizen engagement presuppose government by consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aim not part of the ideology.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not discussed; regulation and taxation imply acceptance of state coercion.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: It values competition rules in markets but pairs competition with social goods; Fish says it rejects survival of the fittest framing.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Liberty and free speech emphasis lean against banning parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Balanced power and decentralization resonate, but the republican concept is not discussed.

separated-powers.rationale: Wikipedia emphasizes balanced power and peer review of decisions.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Minimum income support suggests concern, but priority is not stated.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed; small-property preference and welfare-state leanings point in opposite directions.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from liberty emphasis and left-liberal orientation.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Contrary to tech optimism and social liberalism.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Contradicts social liberalism and networked pluralism.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not discussed, though participatory leanings might incline some adherents.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: It favors competitive markets with enforced rules.

party-controls-media.rationale: Contradicts free speech and free networked communication.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Representative pay is not discussed, though participatory leanings might favor it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Individuality and decentralization lean against binding discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Wikipedia cites EU competition law approvingly, but sovereignty pooling is not stated.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Balanced power emphasis leans against executive concentration.

clerical-rule.rationale: Contrary to faith in technology and liberal governance.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed; liberal pacific leanings but not defeatism.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Balanced power and peer review lean against.

recall-officials.rationale: Citizen engagement and participation lean toward it; not stated.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not covered; liberal internationalism and anti-militarism pull opposite ways.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Supports car-free cities, implying urban orientation.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: It values public education and engineering-style expertise.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Social liberal orientation suggests this; not stated.

death-penalty.rationale: Left-liberal orientation suggests opposition; not discussed.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Left-liberal social orientation plus publicly funded education; not discussed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Technology faith and engineering-style approach contradict it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Free speech and minimal technology controls lean against.

minority-language-support.rationale: Decentralization and inclusion lean toward; not discussed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Accommodating minority religion and applying general law equally both fit liberalism, and the sources are silent.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Its core values are liberty and individuality.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt is not discussed, and left-liberal sympathy competes with rules-based markets.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Post-colonial economics is outside the ideology's sources.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not discussed; public consultation supports deliberation but not this specific mechanism.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid is not addressed; left-liberal sympathy competes with market and tech-transfer emphasis.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from liberal orientation.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Executive selection is not covered; participation favors direct election but balanced power does not.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not covered; rules-based markets suggest independence but nothing is stated.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is not discussed; competition rules for large firms and fair taxes suggest conditional property.

precautionary-principle.rationale: It favors engineering-style regulation and emissions pricing, but also minimal technology controls.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance guarantees are outside the ideology's sources and adherents are split between internationalist and anti-militarist views.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Territorial disputes are not addressed by the sources; liberal norms suggest a view but not one the ideology states.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state relations are not discussed; liberty and secular leanings pull in different ways.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Head-of-state design is not discussed in the sources.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not discussed, though decentralization is sympathetic.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contradicts the technology and individualism worldview.

flat-income-tax.rationale: It favors fair taxation and a negative income tax, which is progressive in effect.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nature-nurture is not addressed, and technology optimism could support either enhancement or environmental views.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Contradicts balanced power and rules-based markets.

space-expansion.rationale: Technology faith makes space ambition plausible; not stated.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Balanced power resonates, but classical mixed constitution is not discussed.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law is not discussed in the sources, and liberal and gender-equality views could differ on a legal presumption.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not discussed; favors small business but not expropriation.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not discussed, and adherents have no common line on it.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not covered; EU competition-law admiration is the only related signal and it is weak.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority institutions are not discussed; decentralization and liberal individualism pull different ways.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority strategy questions are outside the ideology, and the sources do not address them.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Technology as driver resonates but the Marxist frame is not shared.

ban-cartels.rationale: It applies stricter competition rules to large firms and aims to weaken concentrated corporate power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed; rules-based markets suggest skepticism while a social-liberal state suggests pragmatism.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Balanced power and peer review lean against unconstrained majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Left-liberal inclusion lean, but quotas are not discussed.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Cap and trade and fair tax themes suggest favoring standards; not stated for trade.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Contradicts the ideology's participatory, peaceful approach.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Individuality and anti-top-down orientation lean toward; not stated.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Left-liberal orientation suggests keeping preferences; not stated.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not covered by the sources; decentralization is sympathetic but nothing is stated.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: It sees technology as resolving capitalism's tensions, so adherents think it adapts.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Balanced power and liberty emphasis suggest support for entrenched limits on government; constitutional design is not discussed.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial borders are outside the ideology's concerns and the sources say nothing on them.

elective-rulers.rationale: Citizen engagement, consultation and peer review of decisions presuppose chosen rather than hereditary rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Peer review and balanced power do not extend to individual vetoes; a decision rule of this kind is not discussed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Balanced power and rules-based governance suggest lawful resistance to lawless rule; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not addressed; it values balanced power more than any single supreme body.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Left-liberal and technogaian-adjacent orientation suggests agreement, though sources do not cover animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not discussed; adherents are likely split between humane use and abolitionist views.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Fish describes technoliberalism's social responsibility as lip service, but adherents do not formally endorse an aristocratic duty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: It promotes citizen engagement, petitions and consultation, the opposite of withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Fish is critical of media structures but his concern is commercial consolidation, not pacification by culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Fish calls technoliberal media hegemonic or counter-hegemonic, a Gramscian note, but adherents themselves do not state this.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems theory is not part of the ideology.

native-born-offices.rationale: Contradicts liberal individualism and cosmopolitan networks.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist party doctrine is outside this ideology.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not discussed; decentralization and local spending suggest some self-reliance, but trade and tech transfer help.

return-lost-territory.rationale: No irredentist element; inferred from liberal orientation.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Its liberal individualism does not support group-based political leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not discussed; liberal values imply opposition to fascism but not necessarily a constitutional founding value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Historical comparison is outside the ideology, though liberal values oppose both regimes.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Left-liberal orientation leans against this revisionist claim.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Left-liberal orientation, though the topic is not discussed.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gendered policy is not discussed in the sources, and adherents are split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Gender and violence policy is not discussed in the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Universal liberal and networked framing leans against civilizational relativism.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Contradicts balanced power and citizen participation.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care work is not discussed; a basic income might partly serve this, but nothing says so.

filial-duty.rationale: Family duty is not addressed; individualism leans against but nothing is stated.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not discussed, though engineering-style governance might appeal.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Open competition and open networks lean against, though anti-corporate-concentration themes pull the other way.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Participatory tendencies suggest openness but it is not discussed.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not addressed; market choice and welfare floor pull opposite ways.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Balanced power and peer review of decisions suggest support.

land-use-tenure.rationale: It supports markets and small business ownership.

single-official-language.rationale: Liberal pluralism and open networks oppose restrictive language rules.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Open networked and liberal orientation leans against such restrictions.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Left-liberal lean to yes, liberty lean to no; not discussed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not discussed; it favors local spending and environmental pricing, but not criticism of consumption as such.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: No interventionist content; liberal orientation leans against.

corporate-influence.rationale: Fish criticises corporate liberalism and the entrenchment of economic liberalism via Citizens United, and Wikipedia stresses weakening corporate power.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Open networked communication and free speech lean against such controls.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not discussed; liberal individualism leans against state natalism.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local control resonates but openness opposes; not discussed.

job-guarantee.rationale: It prefers a basic income floor to jobs guarantees, but is not explicit.

democratic-peace.rationale: Liberal framing, with the idea that networked tech spreads liberalism, favors this; not stated.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Political obligation is not discussed, and its rule-based, consultative view of government sits uneasily with either answer.

non-intervention.rationale: Not discussed; liberal orientation leans against absolutist non-intervention.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage law is not addressed, and liberty leanings are offset by social-liberal state protections.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in any source.

public-access-to-information.rationale: It supports free internet access, networked communication and public consultation, and favors open government data.

local-production.rationale: Wikipedia says it argues local spending with small firms benefits local economies.

informal-organisation.rationale: Fish urges activists to just make subversive media, which fits informal action, but he also calls for policy intervention.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Legal hierarchy is not addressed; adherents cite EU competition law approvingly but nothing generalizes.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Wikipedia supports deregulating rules that block competition with government services and favors publicly funded education; mixed provision follows.

religion-illusion.rationale: Its sources are about technology and governance and take no position on religion's truth.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: It supports business capitalism of small firms and holds that technology progress yields social goods; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Feminist economics is outside the sources, and technoliberals pair markets with social liberalism rather than structural change.

socialized-care.rationale: Not discussed; market orientation leans against.

treaties-binding.rationale: Indigenous treaty questions are not addressed by the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Decentralization is sympathetic but its preference is small business, not cooperative property.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: It keeps capitalism but wants to reduce corporate capitalism's power, so it is not a clear third way.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Contradicts engineering-style evidence orientation and liberal values.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Contradicts free speech and citizen engagement.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Wikipedia stresses citizen engagement, public consultations and petitions; Fish's book is on participatory culture, though he reports its decline.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional theory is not part of the sources, though left-liberal adherents may be sympathetic.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Fish defines it as reconciling economic and social liberalism, a kind of synthesis, but he does not call left-right obsolete.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist concept not part of the ideology.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The sources are silent; liberty and secularism pull in opposite directions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Social liberalism and transparency; not discussed.

social-market-economy.rationale: It supports free markets with strongly enforced rules, stricter competition rules and a minimum income, matching this formula.

rich-first.rationale: Development strategy is not addressed in the sources.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Great-power alignment is outside the ideology.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Contradicts peer review and balance of power.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: IMF conditionality is not discussed, and adherents have no common position.

property-franchise.rationale: Contradicts liberal values and citizen engagement.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist claims are not part of the sources.

reification.rationale: Marxist concept not part of the ideology.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Fish criticises for-profit media consolidation and a weak public media domain, arguing without legislation and funding social liberalism dissipates.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rules-based markets and balanced power suggest support.

online-participation.rationale: Wikipedia lists networked communication, online speech and engagement with technology as central to the ideology, and cites citizen consultation.

open-government-data.rationale: Peer review of decisions and public consultation imply published records.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Public consultations and peer review of decisions are central to its governance picture.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is outside the ideology's sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Fish criticises corporate liberalism and Wikipedia aims to weaken corporate concentration.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational design is not covered by the sources.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: It supports minimum income and public education over reliance on charity.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed, though balance of power might favor them.

vote-delegation.rationale: Networked participation suggests liquid democracy as a plausible fit, though not stated.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential risk is not discussed, though technology faith may produce both optimism and concern.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not discussed; religion is outside the ideology.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Franchise questions are not addressed; openness leans yes but nothing says so.

rent-control.rationale: It prefers competition and market rules; not discussed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Fish's networked outlook is sympathetic to openness, but creative-industry IP is not addressed.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is not addressed in any source.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign basing is not addressed in any source.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Historical recognition politics is outside the sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Distributional principle is not addressed; basic income runs against work-only reward while competition rules favor effort over rents.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Pacifism is not addressed; liberal individualism generally accepts self-defence, so this leans against.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Gender theory is outside the ideology's sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory is outside the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: No nationalist or religious martyr content.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora politics is outside the sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: Nation-building sequencing is outside the sources.

god-not-male.rationale: Religious language is outside the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Religious feminism is outside the sources.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Administrative boundaries for peoples are outside the sources.

independent-unions.rationale: Union-party relations are not discussed in the sources.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Marxist doctrinal question outside the ideology.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Local utility ownership is not discussed; decentralization favors local provision but markets favor competition.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative structure is not covered, though balance of power might suggest sympathy.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Decentralization is sympathetic but this municipalist structure is not discussed.

family-wage.rationale: It prefers negative income tax or basic income, not employer-borne wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Technology should be widely available with minimal controls, and it supports genetic engineering.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Faith in technology suggests support; not stated.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Free networked communication with minimal controls leans toward; not stated.

online-anonymity.rationale: Free online communication and speech with minimal controls imply anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: Liberty, individuality and responsibility are the founding values.

spiritual-nature.rationale: It is secular and tech oriented.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Decentralization leans against revocable regional autonomy.

gm-crops.rationale: Wikipedia states it supports allowing genetic engineering, including for food.

dense-cities.rationale: It supports car-free cities, which implies dense urban form.

racial-pride.rationale: Not discussed; liberal individualism leans against.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: War policy is not discussed in the sources.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiratorial nationalist claim foreign to the ideology.

free-public-college.rationale: It supports publicly funded education, though tuition-free college specifically is not stated.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Wikipedia states it supports higher taxes on environmentally damaging activity and fossil fuels, and emissions trading.

future-generations.rationale: Environmental pricing implies concern for the future; not stated.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Difference feminism is not addressed in the sources.

arms-reduction.rationale: Disarmament is not addressed in the sources.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Open government and public information themes suggest agreement; diplomacy is not discussed.

capital-controls.rationale: Open networks and markets lean against.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Arms control is not addressed; liberty and security pull opposite ways.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Conscientious refusal is not discussed; liberty leans toward individual conscience but no source says so.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Labor relations are not discussed in the sources.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: A negative income tax, which tops up low incomes via the tax system, is among its listed policies.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are not addressed in the sources.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: International economic order is not discussed in the sources.

smash-state-machine.rationale: It works within government and law through consultation and regulation.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Decentralization is sympathetic but not discussed.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Emissions trading and pollution pricing treat environmental limits through markets.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student debt is not discussed; publicly funded education suggests sympathy but nothing is stated.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Regional exploitation theory is outside the sources, though decentralization might be sympathetic.

shared-human-nature.rationale: It supports human enhancement and genetic engineering, which sit poorly with fixed human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Fish criticises the weakened public media domain and wants legislation and direct funding for the social liberal side.

missingStatements.text: Networked technology can resolve the conflict between free markets and social welfare goals.
missingStatements.rationale: This is the defining claim in Fish's definition of technoliberalism: faith in networked technology to improve both prosperity and social well-being.

notes: Fish treats technoliberalism as a critic describing a discourse, so many adherent positions are inferred from Wikipedia's thin article and general liberal and technology-optimist principles. Most answers are low confidence.
